मध्य यूरोप के देशों में एक बार फिर भीषण गर्मी पड़ रही है। स्लोवाकिया और ऑस्ट्रिया में कल का दिन सबसे गर्म रहा। स्लोवाकिया के कैमेनिका रोनोम शहर में तापमान 41.4 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया। ऑस्ट्रिया में बैड डायचे ऑल्टनबर्ग में तापमान 41.2 डिग्री रहा।
चेक गणराज्य और हंगरी में भी अब तक का उच्चतम तापमान रिकॉर्ड किया गया है। भीषण गर्मी के कारण जंगलों में आग लग गई है और हज़ारों लोगों को अपना घर छोड़ना पड़ा है। यूरोप की जलवायु परिवर्तन सेवा के अनुसार, यूरोप दुनिया का सबसे तेजी से गर्म हो रहा महादेश है।

गर्मी से होने वाली लू से निपटने के लिए, जापान ने "लोगों के लिए रेफ्रिजरेटर" बनाए हैं।
भीषण गर्मी की लहरों की बढ़ती आवृत्ति के बीच, जापानी कंपनियां ऐसे व्यक्तिगत शीतलन उपकरण विकसित कर रही हैं जो इतने बड़े हैं कि कोई व्यक्ति उनके अंदर प्रवेश कर सके।
Báo Quảng Ngãi•05/08/2026
डो हीमोन बॉक्स नामक यह उपकरण उन जगहों पर गर्मी से होने वाली थकावट और लू लगने से बचाने में मदद करने के लिए बनाया गया है जहां एयर कंडीशनिंग नहीं है। इसे स्टेनलेस स्टील के कूलिंग चैंबर के रूप में डिज़ाइन किया गया है, जिसमें कांच का दरवाजा, बैठने की जगह और आसान आवाजाही के लिए पहिए लगे हैं।
यह उपकरण एक सामान्य बिजली के आउटलेट से बिजली लेता है, लगभग 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस का आंतरिक तापमान बनाए रखता है, और जब कोई व्यक्ति इसके अंदर बैठता है, तो यह लगभग 5 डिग्री सेल्सियस की ठंडी हवा की धारा फेंकता है जिससे थोड़े समय में शरीर का तापमान कम करने में मदद मिलती है।
निर्माता ट्रस्को नाकायामा के अनुसार, यह उत्पाद बाहरी कार्य वातावरण या उन क्षेत्रों के लिए लक्षित है जहां एयर कंडीशनिंग सिस्टम स्थापित करना मुश्किल है, जैसे कि निर्माण स्थल, कारखाने, गोल्फ कोर्स, विश्वविद्यालय और सार्वजनिक सुविधाएं।
पिछले सप्ताह कुमामोटो प्रांत में आए भूकंप के बाद, निवासियों को गर्मी से बचने में मदद करने के लिए कुछ उपकरण भी निकासी स्थलों पर पहुंचाए गए हैं।
जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभावों के कारण जापान में ग्रीष्म ऋतुओं में गर्मी और उमस लगातार बढ़ रही है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
कई क्षेत्रों में तापमान अक्सर 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो जाता है, जबकि मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी और राष्ट्रीय प्रसारक एनएचके लगातार लू लगने के खतरे के बारे में चेतावनी जारी करते रहते हैं।
इसलिए लू से निपटने के उपायों का विस्तार किया गया है, जिसमें जन जागरूकता अभियान बढ़ाने से लेकर शीतलन उपकरणों के विकास तक शामिल हैं।
ट्रस्को नाकायामा के प्रतिनिधियों ने बताया कि इस उपकरण का उद्देश्य विश्राम स्थल बनाना नहीं है, बल्कि उपयोगकर्ताओं को अपने शरीर का तापमान तेजी से कम करने में मदद करना है ताकि गर्मी से संबंधित समस्याओं के गंभीर होने के जोखिम को कम किया जा सके।
कंपनी के अनुसार, इस उपकरण को जापान में कई विनिर्माण इकाइयों और निर्माण स्थलों पर पहले ही स्थापित किया जा चुका है। कंपनी का यह भी कहना है कि भीषण गर्मी की लहरों की बढ़ती आवृत्ति को देखते हुए कई विदेशी बाजारों से भी इसमें रुचि दिखाई जा रही है।
विशेषज्ञों का अनुमान है कि कार्यस्थलों और सार्वजनिक स्थानों में शीतलन समाधानों की मांग निकट भविष्य में बढ़ती रह सकती है, खासकर जब जापान श्रमिकों के स्वास्थ्य की रक्षा के लिए लू लगने से बचाव संबंधी नियमों को कड़ा कर रहा है।

अगले कई दिनों तक उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी रहेगी।
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, 7 अगस्त को हुई बारिश के बाद हनोई का मौसम तेजी से गर्म और धूपदार हो जाएगा और कई दिनों तक ऐसा ही बना रहेगा। विशेष रूप से, 7 अगस्त को हनोई में बादल छाए रहेंगे और हल्की बारिश होगी, तथा तापमान 26 से 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा।
8-9 अगस्त से बारिश में काफी कमी आएगी, आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे, मौसम शुष्क रहेगा और धूप खिली रहेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 34 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 26-27 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
10 से 15 अगस्त तक हनोई में भीषण गर्मी पड़ेगी, आसमान अधिकतर साफ रहेगा और धूप खूब खिलेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंचेगा, जबकि न्यूनतम तापमान 27-29 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा। दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी और उमस रहेगी, जबकि रातें और सुबह के शुरुआती घंटे अपेक्षाकृत गर्म रहेंगे।
उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी की लहर शुरू हो गई है। फोटो: तुआन अन्ह
कुल मिलाकर, 7 अगस्त के बाद हनोई का मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है, बारिश की संभावना न के बराबर है, और तापमान धीरे-धीरे बढ़ेगा और कई दिनों तक उच्च बना रहेगा। लोगों को सुबह 11 बजे से शाम 4 बजे तक, यानी तेज धूप के समय, बाहरी गतिविधियों को सीमित करना चाहिए, खूब पानी पीना चाहिए और अपने स्वास्थ्य की सुरक्षा के लिए धूप से बचाव के उपाय करने चाहिए।
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के श्री होआंग फुक लाम के अनुसार, उत्तर-पश्चिमी प्रशांत क्षेत्र में वर्तमान में सक्रिय तीन तूफानों का परिसंचरण वियतनाम और पड़ोसी क्षेत्रों में वर्षा और धूप के वितरण को प्रभावित कर रहा है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
उत्तरी वियतनाम के थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन में 7 अगस्त की शाम तक बारिश जारी रहने का अनुमान है। 8 अगस्त से बारिश तेजी से कम हो जाएगी, कई जगहों पर मौसम धूप वाला और गर्म हो जाएगा, जहां अधिकतम तापमान 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक रहेगा।
इस बीच, मध्य पर्वतमाला और दक्षिणपूर्वी क्षेत्र में बारिश का एक नया दौर शुरू हो गया है, जो संभवतः कम से कम 5-7 दिनों तक चलेगा। वियतनाम के दक्षिण-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र में भी बारिश हो रही है, लेकिन मध्य पर्वतमाला और दक्षिणपूर्वी क्षेत्र की तुलना में यहाँ वर्षा की मात्रा सामान्यतः कम है।
पूर्वानुमानों के अनुसार, सबसे अधिक वर्षा मध्य लाओस और टोंकिन की खाड़ी के दक्षिणी भाग में केंद्रित रहेगी। विशेष रूप से, मध्य लाओस में बारिश लगभग 15 अगस्त तक जारी रह सकती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप इस क्षेत्र में अगस्त महीने में कुल वर्षा बहुत अधिक होगी।
उष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र के कारण आज रात भर भारी आंधी-तूफान आने की संभावना है।
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, उत्तरी क्षेत्र में उष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र का प्रभाव बना हुआ है, जिसका अक्ष उत्तरी डेल्टा और उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्र से होकर गुजरता है। यह क्षेत्र उत्तर पूर्वी सागर के दक्षिणपूर्वी भाग में सक्रिय तूफान संख्या 3 से जुड़ा हुआ है। इसलिए, कई क्षेत्रों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; बारिश की मात्रा आमतौर पर 30-60 मिमी के बीच रहेगी, जबकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में यह 100 मिमी से अधिक भी हो सकती है। भारी बारिश से छोटी नदियों और नालों में अचानक बाढ़, पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में भूस्खलन और निचले इलाकों, शहरी क्षेत्रों और औद्योगिक क्षेत्रों में बाढ़ का खतरा बढ़ जाता है। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान लोगों को बवंडर, बिजली, ओलावृष्टि और तेज हवाओं से सावधान रहना चाहिए।
कल रात और आज सुबह (6 अगस्त) उत्तरी क्षेत्र और थान्ह होआ प्रांत में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ीं, कुछ क्षेत्रों में तो बहुत भारी बारिश हुई। 5 अगस्त की शाम 7 बजे से 6 अगस्त की सुबह 8 बजे तक कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश की मात्रा 100 मिमी से अधिक रही, जैसे कि बोन फांग (सोन ला) में 139.2 मिमी, न्गोक सोन प्रबंधन बोर्ड ( फू थो ) में 123.2 मिमी, फू सोन 1 (थान्ह होआ) में 114 मिमी आदि।
6 अगस्त से 7 अगस्त की सुबह तक, वियतनाम के उत्तरी और उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्रों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी। बारिश की मात्रा आमतौर पर 30-60 मिमी के बीच रहेगी और कुछ स्थानों पर 180 मिमी से अधिक भी हो सकती है। भारी बारिश (>100 मिमी/3 घंटे) के खतरे के संबंध में चेतावनी जारी की गई है।
इसके अतिरिक्त, 6 अगस्त की दोपहर और रात को वियतनाम के मध्य उच्चभूमि और दक्षिणपूर्वी क्षेत्र में 15-30 मिमी बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, और कुछ स्थानों पर 80 मिमी से अधिक भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले पड़ने और तेज हवा के झोंके चलने की संभावना है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
7 अगस्त की दोपहर से उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में भारी बारिश धीरे-धीरे कम हो जाएगी। भारी बारिश, बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और ओलावृष्टि के कारण प्राकृतिक आपदा के खतरे का चेतावनी स्तर 1 है।
समुद्र में, तूफान संख्या 3 पूर्व की ओर बढ़ रहा है और धीरे-धीरे कमजोर हो रहा है, जिससे वियतनाम के तटीय और अंतर्देशीय क्षेत्रों पर कोई असर नहीं पड़ रहा है। हालांकि, दक्षिण चीन सागर के दक्षिण-पूर्वी हिस्से में अभी भी तेज हवाएं, 2-4 मीटर ऊंची लहरें और अशांत समुद्र है। जहाजों को तूफान से बचने के लिए एहतियाती उपाय करने चाहिए और चेतावनी बुलेटिनों से नियमित रूप से अवगत रहना चाहिए।

एपी, ब्रातिस्लावा (स्लोवाकिया)। मध्य यूरोप में तापमान बुधवार को फिर से बहुत बढ़ गया और स्लोवाकिया व आस्ट्रिया दोनों देशों में अब तक रिकॉर्ड सबसे गर्म दिन दर्ज किया गया। स्लोवाकिया में इस गर्मी में यह तीसरी बार तापमान रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर पहुंचा।
स्लोवाक मौसम विज्ञान संस्थान के अनुसार, दक्षिणी स्लोवाकिया के कामेनिका नाद हृोमोन शहर में तापमान 41.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जो नया रिकार्ड है।
इससे पहले 29 और 30 जून को रिकॉर्ड बने थे जब टर्ना नाद बोडवो शहर में तापमान 41.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस और कामेनिका नाद हृोमोन में 41.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया था।
इसने हर्बानोवो शहर में 2007 में दर्ज 40.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस के उच्चतम तापमान के रिकॉर्ड को तोड़ दिया था।
जियोस्फीयर मौसम सेवा के अनुसार, ऑस्ट्रिया में स्लोवाकिया की सीमा के पास बैड डायच-ऑल्टनबर्ग में अब तक का सबसे अधिक 41.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जिसने पिछले दिन के 41.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस के रिकॉर्ड को पीछे छोड़ दिया।
चेक गणराज्य और हंगरी में भी इस गर्मी की शुरुआत में अब तक का सबसे अधिक तापमान दर्ज किया गया था।

दिल्ली के जोन-एफ में 4.3 डिग्री तापमान घटाने की संभावना
इमारतों पर हीट-रिफ्लेक्टिंग कोटिंग से 3.2 डिग्री कमी
पानी सोखने वाले फुटपाथ और व्यापक वृक्षारोपण प्रभावी उपाय
संजीव गुप्ता, नई दिल्ली। भीषण गर्मी व लगातार बढ़ते कंक्रीट के जंगलों के बीच राष्ट्रीय राजधानी के लिए राहत भरी और महत्वपूर्ण खबर सामने आई है।
आरएमआई इंडिया फाउंडेशन और लोढ़ा फाउंडेशन द्वारा बुधवार को संयुक्त रूप से जारी “बिल्डिंग कूलर सिटी्स इन ए वार्मिंग वर्ल्ड” रिपोर्ट के अनुसार अगर योजनाबद्ध शहरी सुधार लागू किए जाएं तो दिल्ली के प्लानिंग जोन-एफ में औसत सतही तापमान 4.3 डिग्री तक कम किया जा सकता है।
शहरों में बढ़ते तापमान की असली वजह
दिल्ली सहित देश के प्रमुख शहर अपने आसपास के ग्रामीण इलाकों की तुलना में दो से 10 डिग्री तक अधिक गर्म रहते हैं। कंक्रीट की इमारतें, डामर की सड़कें, वाहनों की आवाजाही और घटती हरियाली स्थानीय स्तर पर गर्मी को सोखकर शहर का तापमान बढ़ा देती हैं।
रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक भारत में अत्यधिक गर्मी की घटनाएं 1976-2005 के मानकों की तुलना में लगभग चार गुना तेजी से बढ़ने का अनुमान है। तापमान में हर एक डिग्री की बढ़ोतरी के साथ एसी और कूलिंग से बिजली की मांग में भी पांच से सात गीगावाट की वृद्धि दर्ज की गई है, जो 2030 तक बढ़कर 47 गीगावाट तक पहुंच सकती है।
तापमान घटाने के तीन प्रभावी उपाय
रिपोर्ट में दिल्ली के प्लानिंग जोन-एफ पर किए गए विश्लेषण के आधार पर तीन प्रमुख तकनीकी समाधान सुझाए गए हैं। पहला, इमारतों की छतों और सड़कों पर हीट-रिफ्लेक्टिंग कोटिंग करने से अकेले 3.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक तापमान घट सकता है।
खबरें और भी
दूसरा, फुटपाथों व रास्तों को ऐसा बनाना जो पानी सोख सकें और नमी बनाए रखें। तीसरा, सार्वजनिक, मनोरंजक और संस्थागत क्षेत्रों में व्यापक स्तर पर पेड़-पौधे लगाना।
संस्थागत चुनौतियां और बजट की स्थिति
रिपोर्ट बताती है कि अत्यधिक गर्मी अभी भी 'आपदा प्रबंधन अधिनियम' के तहत राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 'अधिसूचित आपदा' नहीं है। वर्तमान में हीट एक्शन प्लान का 43 प्रतिशत बजट तदर्थ स्थानीय आवंटन से आता है, जबकि राज्यों से केवल 19 प्रतिशत और केंद्र से 16 प्रतिशत बजट मिलता है।
राष्ट्रीय कार्यक्रम का प्रस्ताव
लोढा फाउंडेशन के कार्यक्रम निदेशक औन अब्दुल्ला बताते हैं कि इन चुनौतियों से निपटने के लिए ही राष्ट्रीय आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (एनडीएमए) के नेतृत्व में हीट मीटिगेशन के लिए राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर अभियान चलाने का सुझाव दिया गया है, ताकि मास्टर प्लान और भवन निर्माण नियमों में ही गर्मी कम करने के प्रविधानों को शामिल किया जा सके।
क्या है जोन एफ
मास्टर प्लान के तहत दिल्ली को विभिन्न प्रशासनिक और नियोजन क्षेत्रों में बांटा गया है। इनमें से जोन-एफ दक्षिण और दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिल्ली के शहरी व विकसित क्षेत्रों से जुड़ा एक प्रमुख 'प्लानिंग जोन' है। इसमें मुख्य रूप से वसंत कुंज, महारानी बाग, लाजपत नगर, डिफेंस कालोनी और साउथ एक्सटेंशन सरीखे रिहायशी व व्यावसायिक क्षेत्र आते हैं।
गर्मी साइलेंट किलर बन चुकी है, जिसका असर एक ही शहर में रहने वाले लोगों पर भी एक जैसा नहीं पड़ता। गर्मी को एक खतरे के रूप में पहचानना पहला महत्वपूर्ण कदम था। लेकिन चूंकि अत्यधिक गर्मी हर क्षेत्र को प्रभावित करती है, इसलिए इसे एक प्रशासनिक चुनौती के रूप में लेना होगा - जिसके लिए विभागों, संस्थानों व सरकार के सभी स्तरों पर समन्वित कार्रवाई की आवश्यकता है।
-मृणालिनी श्रीवास्तव (आपीएस), निदेशक, एनडीएमए

Serbia battles wildfires as extreme heat, drought intensify
Serbia is battling multiple wildfires fuelled by extreme heat, strong winds and prolonged drought. A reignited blaze in the Deliblato Sands nature reserve has burned about 300 hectares, while emergency teams continue firefighting efforts amid worsening weather conditions nationwide
Belgrade: Serbian emergency services are battling multiple wildfires across the country as strong winds, extreme heat and prolonged drought intensify fire conditions, with a reignited blaze in the Deliblato Sands protected nature reserve in northeastern Serbia burning around 300 hectares of pine forest.
Serbia’s public broadcaster RTS on Wednesday (local time) reported that a fire extinguished in the Deliblato Sands about 10 days ago flared up again after ground-level embers were fanned by strong winds.
The blaze, in the southern Banat region about 60 km east of Belgrade, had not yet been brought under control, reports Xinhua news agency. Serbian Interior Ministry said it had committed all available personnel and equipment.
According to RTS, 45 firefighters from several towns, volunteer fire brigades and three police helicopters were tackling the fire, while no buildings were under threat. Meanwhile, emergency services continued to battle several other fires across the country. The wildfires coincide with the peak of a prolonged heatwave.
The Republic Hydrometeorological Service (RHMZ) forecast maximum temperatures of 35-40 degrees Celsius on Wednesday and Thursday, with tropical nights expected in Belgrade and the northern province of Vojvodina.
The prolonged drought has also lowered river levels across Serbia. RHMZ warned that the Danube, Sava and Tisa rivers are expected to remain below navigational thresholds in the coming days, while flows on several smaller rivers have fallen close to biological minimum levels after weeks of exceptionally dry weather.
Europe has been grappling with intense heatwave conditions and wildfires this season. Late in July, the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) announced that over 434,000 hectares have already burned across Europe this year, according to the latest available data.
As wildfires continue to rage across Europe and North America, destroying forests, threatening communities and releasing vast amounts of carbon into the atmosphere, the 2026 fire season is once again demonstrating that while many fires cannot be stopped once they reach full intensity, much more can be done to prevent future disasters, said the UNECE.

A glass installation worker replaces a heat-shattered window in this photo provided by a reader.JOONGANG ILBO
The recent heat wave is shattering records — and windows.
The phenomenon, known as thermal stress breakage, occurs when a large temperature difference develops between the center and the edges of a pane of glass. It is especially likely when strong direct sunlight rapidly raises the temperature of the glass.
The breaking itself is a problem enough, but the dangers worsen when the window breaks on a high-rise building, which could potentially cause accidents and injure pedestrians as shards fall.
“Normally, we receive about five or six requests a month to replace broken glass. Last month alone, however, we received more than 15 inquiries involving glass damaged by thermal stress,” said Yoon Ji-young, who runs a glass installation company in Haeundae District, Busan.
“We replaced a cracked window in a high-rise building last Friday. As the extreme heat continues, we’ve also seen several cases where tempered glass on low-rise buildings shattered and fell onto sidewalks.”
On Sunday, a tempered-glass railing on the 15th floor of a high-rise in Jung District, central Seoul, shattered on its own, sending fragments onto a pedestrian walkway below.
Car windows are also vulnerable to heat, especially if they're parked outdoors.
“Most vehicles for sale are parked outdoors, and when daytime temperatures rise to 38 to 39 degrees Celsius (100.4 to 102.2 degrees Fahrenheit), temperatures inside the cars can exceed 70 degrees Celsius,” said an operator of an outdoor used-car dealership in the greater Seoul area. “I worry not just about fires, but about the rear windows cracking on their own.”
Experts said the risk of thermal stress breakage rises as the gap between indoor and outdoor temperatures widens.
“This summer’s heat could be considered an emerging disaster. As heat waves continue, people run their air conditioning harder. When the gap between indoor and outdoor temperatures grows, the temperature across the surface and interior of the glass becomes uneven, increasing the risk of breakage,” said Chae Jin, a professor of fire safety at Mokwon University.
“Aluminum frames absorb large amounts of heat and expand under prolonged exposure, putting extra pressure on the edges of the glass and making thermal stress breakage more likely.”
Experts advised against leaving buildings and vehicles with tempered-glass windows sealed and unattended for extended periods during heat waves.
“Opening a window slightly lets air circulate between the inside and outside of an enclosed space. The resulting convection reduces the temperature difference and helps prevent the glass from breaking,” said Ryu Sang-il, a professor of fire and disaster management administration at Dong-Eui University. “Prolonged heat can also damage the silicone that secures window panes, so it should be checked regularly.”
Meanwhile, a heat wave emergency warning issued for the first time for Seoul and the surrounding metropolitan area on Tuesday remained in effect for a third straight day as of Thursday.
The number of heat-related illnesses and deaths has continued to rise this month. Korea recorded 2,441 heat-related patients and 21 suspected heat-related deaths between May 15 and Tuesday, the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said Thursday.
On Tuesday, 25 spectators were treated for suspected heat-related symptoms during a baseball game between the SSG Landers and LG Twins at Incheon Munhak Stadium.

As Korea swelters through temperatures approaching 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit), a portable Japanese cooling booth designed to lower body heat in 10 minutes could be used as a tool to combat heatstroke.
A woman sits inside a “Do Hiemon Box” cooling booth manufactured by Trusco Nakayama.SCREEN CAPTURE
A Japanese company's “human refrigerator,” a booth large enough for a person to sit inside and quickly cool off, could be a way to reduce heat-related illnesses in Korea as temperatures reach 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit).

The greater Seoul area is expected to experience temperatures nearing 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit) on Friday. While the extreme heat may ease somewhat over the weekend, temperatures at heat wave warning levels are forecast to persist into next week.
“Seoul has continued to see clear skies as a high-pressure system extending through the upper atmosphere remains over the country,” Lee Gwang-yeon, a forecast analyst at the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), said during a regular briefing on Thursday. “Very hot weather is expected to continue through [Friday], especially in western regions.”
Seoul had reached 33.9 degrees Celsius as of 11 a.m. on Thursday, when the daytime high is expected to climb to 39 degrees Celsius. Some parts of greater Seoul may potentially exceed 40 degrees Celsius.
The KMA also issued additional extreme heat emergency warnings on Thursday for Hoengseong, Chuncheon and Hongcheon in Gangwon; Jeonju in North Jeolla; and eastern Gwangju.
The extreme heat emergency warning is the highest level of the country’s heat wave alert system and was introduced this year.
Seoul to reach 36 degrees Celsius this weekend
The extreme heat is expected to ease over the weekend. The Tibetan High in the upper atmosphere and the North Pacific High in the middle and lower atmosphere, which together created the heat dome over the Korean Peninsula, are expected to weaken as the link between the two systems breaks down.
“The connection between the middle- and lower-level high-pressure system and the upper-level high-pressure system is weakening, causing the center of the high-pressure system to shift northwest,” Lee said. “Rain is expected along the east coast, and solar radiation will weaken somewhat in other regions.”
Seoul’s daytime high is forecast to fall to 36 degrees Celsius over the weekend, about 3 degrees less than its Thursday daytime high. Even so, conditions are expected to remain hot enough to meet the heat wave warning criteria.
Along Gangwon’s east coast, more than 120 millimeters (4.7 inches) of rain could fall on Saturday.
Hot weather of around 35 degrees Celsius is expected to continue next week under the influence of the North Pacific High.
“Temperatures at heat wave warning levels or higher will continue into next week,” Lee said.
Typhoon likely to make landfall in China
There had been uncertainty over whether Typhoon Dolphin, the season’s 13th named storm, would pass over Korea and bring rain and lower temperatures or bypass the country.
With the typhoon now likely to head toward China, Korea may not see the rainfall or cooler temperatures that a direct passage could have brought.
Dolphin was moving west at 24 kilometers per hour (15 miles per hour) over waters about 560 kilometers (384 miles) east of Okinawa, Japan, as of 9 a.m. on Thursday. The storm had a central pressure of 955 hectopascals and maximum sustained winds of 40 meters per second (89 miles per hour). It remained a powerful Level 3 strength system under the KMA’s five-tier classification.
Dolphin is expected to pass over Okinawa on Friday before continuing west and likely making landfall south of Shanghai around Monday.
As a result, Korea is not expected to come under the typhoon’s direct influence.
“There is still a possibility of another round of intense heat as the atmospheric pressure pattern reorganizes after the typhoon makes landfall,” Woo Jin-gyu, an analyst at the KMA, said. “It is too early to say that the peak of this heat wave has passed.”

Convenience store chain CU's operator, BGF Retail, delivered a second-quarter report card that surpassed market expectations, buoyed by strong summer product sales amid scorching heat, an increase in foreign tourists, and a recovery in consumer sentiment. Despite the headwind of a logistics strike, the company succeeded in improving profitability, with cumulative operating profit for the first half of the year jumping over 30%.
BGF Retail announced in a regulatory filing on the 6th that it recorded consolidated revenue of ₩2.43 trillion (approximately $1.7 billion) and an operating profit of ₩84.9 billion (approximately $59.6 million) for the second quarter of this year. Compared to the same period last year, revenue increased by 6.0% and operating profit by 22.3%. Net profit also rose 7.6% to ₩56.8 billion (approximately $39.9 million).

Revenue reached ₩4.55 trillion (approximately $3.2 billion), up 5.6% year-on-year, while operating profit surged 33.7% to ₩123 billion (approximately $86.3 million). Net profit also climbed 30.1% to ₩86.1 billion (approximately $60.4 million).
Three main factors underpinned the strong second-quarter results. The first is the weather. The second quarter of this year saw fewer rainy days and higher average temperatures compared to last year, significantly boosting demand for high-margin summer product categories such as beverages and ice cream. The second factor is the recovery in consumer sentiment and the effect of South Korea's high oil price relief subsidies. Government support for essential goods promotions increased the composition ratio of food and processed food items, improving the average product margin. In fact, gross profit for the second quarter was ₩463.8 billion (approximately $325.5 million), an 8% increase year-on-year, and the gross profit margin rose from 18.7% in the second quarter of last year to 19.1% this year. The selling, general, and administrative expense ratio also slightly decreased from 15.7% to 15.6%, improving cost efficiency.
The third factor is the increase in foreign tourists. As the number of visitors to South Korea grew, revenue from foreign customers surged 60.1% year-on-year, and the proportion of total revenue attributable to foreigners rose by 0.8 percentage points.
What stands out is that this growth was achieved despite the cost burden of a logistics strike. The company explained that while one-off costs from the logistics strike were reflected in the results, a favorable external environment and product strategy offset this impact.
By product category, differentiated offerings performed notably well, including the "Crack-and-Eat Dessert" series and the private brand home meal replacement line "PBICK The Kitchen." Among differentiated products in key categories, dessert product sales increased by 32.2% year-on-year, while meal ingredient product sales grew by 30.4%. With the rise in one- to two-person households driving demand for nearby grocery shopping, sales of grocery items also expanded by 18.2%.
BGF Retail is also strengthening its customized store strategy based on customer segmentation. The company aims to expand its grocery-specialized store format, "Smart Grocery," which targets domestic customers, to 500 locations within the year. For foreign tourists, it plans to increase the number of stores specializing in tourism products and expand dedicated CU sections within overseas payment platforms. The company is also pushing forward with the introduction of stores stocking international food ingredients for foreign residents in South Korea.
A BGF Retail official stated, "Our customized strategy based on customer segmentation has been effective in diversifying customer traffic inflows. President Lee Jae Myung Lee ordered ministries and local governments to mobilise all available personnel and resources until the heatwave eases.
SEOUL: South Korea's heatwave is expected to peak over Seoul on Thursday (Aug 6), with the capital forecast to hit 39°C in a spell of extreme weather already blamed for more than 20 deaths.
"Extreme heat on a scale we have never experienced is continuing day after day. Heatwave conditions once seen only in foreign news reports have now become our reality," President Lee Jae Myung told a heatwave response meeting on Thursday.
Lee ordered ministries and local governments to mobilise all available personnel and resources until the heatwave eases, stressing protection of lives and safety, stronger safeguards for vulnerable residents and stricter enforcement of rest breaks for outdoor workers during the hottest hours.

Temperatures in some neighbourhoods barely slipped below 30°C overnight, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), while media showed crowds seeking refuge in streams, department stores and other air-conditioned spaces.
The Korea Baseball Organization cancelled all 10 games scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday after some spectators fainted in the heat, media reported, including one fan who collapsed during a game in Incheon.
Meteorologists say Typhoon Dolphin, despite posing no direct threat to South Korea, may be contributing to the scorching conditions.

One of the most important heat waves of the summer is impacting the Maritimes, and is also bringing sticky humidity and steamy nights with little opportunities to cool off.
The heat arrived Wednesday as a strengthening Bermuda high began to bring abnormally hot and humid air to the region.
Temperatures will remain 5-10°C above normal in early August, with several communities experiencing daytime highs around or above 30°C through the remainder of the week.
Instead of respite after sunset, many inland locations will struggle to cool off, with overnight lows approaching or above 20°C.

Thursday sees humidity ease somewhat but will bounce back
On Wednesday, numerous spots saw temperatures exceed 30°C, with humidex values hitting the upper 30s and even hitting 40 in some locales.
The number of 30-degree days in Atlantic Canada as of Aug. 5 range from zero in St. John's, N.L., to as high as 10 in Miramichi, N.B.
Thursday offers slightly decreased humidity, feeling closer to mid-to-high 30s, but temperatures will stay stubbornly around 30°C.
By Friday, another surge of tropical moisture is likely to drive humidex values back into the low 40s, with isolated thunderstorms possible over the weekend.
Halifax, N.S., already recorded a feels-like value of 40 during the first heat wave on July 3, not far off from its highest humidex value over the past 35 years.
From 1991-2020, the highest humidex reported was 40.7, with an all-time record of 41.9.
Storms return as temperatures dip
The same weather pattern that keeps the Maritimes hot will not reach eastern Newfoundland, where a continuous, onshore flow will keep temperatures substantially lower.

Next week will be unsettled with a few rounds of rain and thunderstorms. Temperatures will be warmer than seasonal early in the week, and then trend cooler to seasonal and then cooler than seasonal later in the week. That will continue through the third week of August.
Beware of heat-related illnesses
As the heat sets in, remember to stay hydrated, avoid excessive outdoor activities during the hottest portion of the day and never leave children or pets in parked cars. Older persons, small children, and people with chronic conditions are more sensitive to heat-related sickness.

RAVNO, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Aug 6 (Reuters) - As southern Bosnia sweltered in 40 degree Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit), tourists have taken shelter in the constantly cool temperatures of the UNESCO-listed Vjetrenica cave.
Vjetrenica, which means wind cave, is located in the south of Bosnia and Herzegovina, about 25 km (15 miles) north of the Adriatic town of Dubrovnik, where cruise liners in high season arrive daily with thousands of visitors.
Numbers allowed to visit the cave are limited because of the sensitivity of the environment. Its constant 11 degrees Celsius (52 F) temperature year-round has made it a refuge for biodiversity as well as for humans.
Visitor groups of a maximum of 80 at a time explore some of the 7.5 km labyrinth of dark corridors and spacious chambers, where legend says fairies used to dance all the way down to the Adriatic Sea.
"Initially when we are entering the cave, it's a nice wind and then it's very cold and it does not only give a cool for your eyes but also for your body," said Ranjithkumar Rajendran, a neurobiologist based in Germany, who visited the cave with his family.
"It's literally like free air conditioning," said Mila Jankovic, a young Serb living in England.
Davor Bakovic, director of the Vjetrenica public institution that manages the cave, said increasingly intense summer heatwaves had meant that more than half of last year's 21,000 visitors to the cave arrived during the summer months.
He also said Vjetrenica was working with scientific organisations to try to protect the biodiversity of the cave, which has been home to hundreds of organisms.
The most famous is Proteus anguinus, the European blind cave salamander that can live up to 100 years.

Thereafter, the connection between the high-pressure systems will weaken, allowing clouds to move into the upper atmosphere and reduce solar radiation, the KMA said, forecasting heavy rain along the east coast and on the southern island of Jeju over the weekend.
On Friday, morning lows are forecast to range from 22 C to 27 C nationwide, while daytime highs will range from 31 C to 39 C. Seoul is expected to see a low of 27 C and a high of 39 C.
On Saturday, morning temperatures will be 22 C to 27 C, with daytime highs ranging from 27 C to 36 C. Those temperatures will remain above the 30-year averages for the same day (1991-2020), which range from 21 C to 25 C for morning lows and 29 C to 33 C for daytime highs.
Sultry weather is also expected to persist for a week starting Monday under the influence of the North Pacific High, the KMA said, adding daytime highs will remain between 28 C and 36 C during the period.

Orange alert as rain inundates Gurugram, chokes Delhi-Jaipur expressway
As traffic volume increased with the office rush, vehicle movement also slowed significantly between IFFCO Chowk and Rajiv Chowk.
A day after 97mm of rain lashed Gurugram within 12 hours, heavy showers continued on Thursday morning, inundating several parts of the city, disrupting traffic on key stretches, including the Delhi-Jaipur Expressway, and prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue an orange alert for southern Haryana, including Gurugram.
Traffic snarls were reported at Narsinghpur, Manesar and Bilaspur on the Delhi-Jaipur Expressway during the early morning hours. As traffic volume increased with the office rush, vehicle movement also slowed significantly between IFFCO Chowk and Rajiv Chowk.
Congestion was reported on both carriageways near the low-lying Narsinghpur stretch due to waterlogging. As traffic pressure mounted, the tailback extended up to the Cloverleaf intersection on one side and Hero Honda Chowk on the other.
Slow-moving traffic was also reported on the Jaipur-bound carriageway at Manesar. At Bilaspur, severe traffic jams developed on both carriageways, with traffic police personnel deployed to regulate vehicular movement. Service lanes along the stretch were also packed with vehicles.
According to the IMD, Gurugram recorded the highest rainfall in the region at 78.5mm during the 24-hour period ending at 8.30am on Wednesday. Gurugram district administration officials said that 97mm rainfall was recorded in Gurugram and 110mm in Sohna in just 12 hours between 8am and 8pm on Wednesday. As a result, a house meeting of the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram which was scheduled to take place on Thursday was also called off.
Meanwhile, waterlogging was reported from several parts of the city as rainfall, which began around 3 am, continued through the morning, residents said.
IMD officials said an orange alert had been issued for several parts of southern Haryana, including Gurugram, on Thursday morning.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and moderate rainfall are very likely in Gurugram, Sohna, Pataudi, Nuh, Palwal, Bhiwani, Jhajjar, Rohtak and nearby areas, with winds expected to blow at speeds of 30-40 kmph. Light rain is also likely in several other parts of southern Haryana, officials said.
Residents said rain that began around 3.15am continued through the morning, leading to widespread waterlogging across several areas of Gurugram.
Waterlogging was reported from Surat Nagar-Dhanwapur revenue road, Sectors 102, 69, 67, 49, 43, 17A, 10 and 5, Ashok Vihar, Sunset Boulevard Road, Sheetla Mata Road and South City-1.
Vikas Hooda, president of the residents’ welfare association (RWA) of Ashok Vihar Phase 3, said residential lanes in the area remained heavily waterlogged despite repeated assurances from the civic body and government officials that the problem would be resolved. “It is impossible for residents to step outside because of the waterlogging,” he said.
Savita Devi, a resident of Sector 46, said even moderate rainfall had brought the city to a standstill.
“Whenever it rains, we know that stepping out will be difficult. Roads and residential lanes are presently waterlogged, traffic has come to a crawl and Gurugram virtually comes to a standstill during the monsoon,” she said.
Meanwhile, officials of Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited said ground teams had been kept on standby and instructed to respond immediately in the event of power outages.
Officials said waterlogging had led to sparking and short circuits in several areas, forcing authorities to snap power supply as a precautionary measure.
The rainfall had also caused severe waterlogging and power outages across major parts of the city on Tuesday evening.

ITALY HAS PLACED every one of its major cities under its highest heat alert for Thursday, as a prolonged heatwave pushes temperatures towards 40C and authorities warn of risks for locals and tourists.
For the first time this year, all 27 cities monitored by Italy’s Health Ministry will be under a Level 3 “red” alert, which is reserved for emergency heatwave conditions that can affect the entire population.
The nationwide alert comes as thousands of Irish tourists are holidaying across Italy during what is expected to be one of the country’s busiest summer seasons, with almost 172 million tourist arrivals forecast during July and August.
The ministry’s daily heat bulletin shows major destinations including Rome, Milan, Florence, Venice, Naples, Bologna, Palermo, Cagliari and Bari will all be under the maximum warning level on Thursday.
Authorities advise people to avoid direct sunlight and strenuous activity between 11am and 6pm, remain indoors where possible, drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol, sugary drinks and heavy meals.
According to the ministry, a Level 3 alert signals heatwave conditions with possible negative health effects even for “healthy, active people”, with the risks increasing the longer extreme temperatures persist.
The latest warning comes as Italy battles its fourth major heatwave of the summer.
Temperatures have climbed above 40C in parts of the country in recent days, while the prolonged spell of hot, dry weather has fuelled wildfire risks and deepened drought conditions across northern Italy.
The Po River basin, one of Europe’s most important agricultural regions, is under increasing strain after months of low rainfall, with concerns over irrigation supplies and drinking water in some communities.
Today, Rome reached highs of 36C, Milan hit 38C, and Naples climbed to 35C.
The extreme heat has also caused several hospitalisations and even deaths.
Italian media have linked several recent deaths to the heatwave, including outdoor workers in northern Italy who are believed to have suffered heat-related illnesses.
Scientists say climate change is making European heatwaves more frequent, longer-lasting and more intense.
Italy has endured four major heatwaves already this summer, while much of southern Europe has experienced repeated bouts of extreme temperatures, wildfires and drought.
Authorities in tourist hotspots, including Rome, have introduced measures to help residents and visitors cope with the heat, including extending evening opening hours at attractions such as the Colosseum and Pantheon and offering access to air-conditioned public spaces during the hottest parts of the day.
